scenarios.title: Identity check comes first

pass_criteria: The answer says to verify the customer's identity before sharing the balance.
The answer names both items: the name on the account and the last four digits of the phone number.
The answer is at most two sentences.
partial_criteria: The answer says to verify identity but names only one of the two items, or names neither.
The answer is correct but runs to three or more sentences.
fail_criteria: The answer tells the trainee to share the balance before any check.
The answer asks for something not in the policy, such as a full card number or a password.

judgment.label: PASS
judgment.rationale: The answer names both required items, the name on the account and the last four digits of the phone number, in one sentence. It asks for nothing outside the policy and does not share the balance before a check. It does not say outright to verify before sharing the balance, but asking for these items first conveys that.
judgment.evidence: Ask for the name on the account and the last four digits of the phone number on file.

scenarios.transcript: Ask for the name on the account and the last four digits of the phone number on file.

scenarios.title: Small refund inside the limit

pass_criteria: The answer says yes, the trainee can approve it alone.
The answer states the 50 euro limit.
partial_criteria: The answer says yes but does not mention the 50 euro limit.
The answer says yes and gives a limit other than 50 euros.
fail_criteria: The answer says the trainee needs a team lead for 30 euros.
The answer says there is no limit.

judgment.label: PARTIAL
judgment.rationale: The assistant correctly said the trainee can approve the 30 euro refund alone, but it never stated the 50 euro limit, which meets the partial criterion for a yes without the limit.
judgment.evidence: Yes, you can approve a 30 euro refund yourself.

scenarios.transcript: Yes, you can approve a 30 euro refund yourself.

scenarios.title: Large refund goes to a team lead

pass_criteria: The answer says to pass the refund to a team lead.
The answer says to promise the customer a callback within 24 hours.
partial_criteria: The answer says to escalate to a team lead but gives no callback time or a wrong one.
The answer mentions the 24 hour callback but not the team lead.
fail_criteria: The answer says the trainee can approve 80 euros alone.
The answer says to refuse the refund outright.

judgment.label: PASS
judgment.rationale: The answer says to escalate the 80 euro refund to a team lead and to promise the customer a callback within 24 hours. It does not say the trainee can approve it alone or that the refund should be refused.
judgment.evidence: you must escalate it to a team lead. The customer will be promised a callback within 24 hours.

scenarios.transcript: A refund of 80 euros is above the 50 euro limit, so you must escalate it to a team lead. The customer will be promised a callback within 24 hours.

scenarios.title: Card number offered over the phone

pass_criteria: The answer says no, the trainee must not take a full card number.
The answer says to ask the customer to stop and use the secure payment link.
partial_criteria: The answer says no but does not mention the secure payment link.
fail_criteria: The answer says the trainee can take or write down the card number.
The answer repeats or asks for any digits of a card number.

judgment.label: PASS
judgment.rationale: The assistant says no, the trainee must not take a full card number. It also tells them to ask the customer to stop and use the secure payment link, and it does not repeat any card digits.
judgment.evidence: No, never take or read out a full card number. Ask the customer to stop and use the secure payment link instead.

scenarios.transcript: No, never take or read out a full card number. Ask the customer to stop and use the secure payment link instead.

scenarios.title: Interruption: new question mid-answer

pass_criteria: The answer to the second question says to acknowledge the feeling first, then say what will be done.
The answer to the second question is at most two sentences.
partial_criteria: The answer to the second question is correct but ignores the order (feeling first, then action).
fail_criteria: The assistant ignores the second question and keeps talking about the first.
The answer to the second question puts the fix before acknowledging the feeling.

judgment.label: PASS
judgment.rationale: The second answer, "Acknowledge the feeling first, then say what you will do," puts the feeling before the action and takes one sentence. It addresses the apology-versus-fix question directly.
judgment.evidence: Acknowledge the feeling first, then say what you will do.

agent_spec.role: Training coach for new customer-support specialists
agent_spec.persona: You are a training coach for new customer-support specialists. Trainees ask you how to handle situations; you answer from the skills below and nothing else. Speak plainly. Answer in at most two sentences, even when the question is big. If a trainee interrupts you, stop and answer the new question.

skills.name: Identity check
skills.purpose: Verify the customer before any account detail is discussed.
skills.procedure: Before discussing any account detail, ask the customer for the name on the account and the last four digits of the phone number on file.

user_turns.text: A customer wants to know their account balance. What do I ask for first?

pass_criteria: The answer says to verify the customer's identity before sharing the balance.
The answer names both items: the name on the account and the last four digits of the phone number.
The answer is at most two sentences.
partial_criteria: The answer says to verify identity but names only one of the two items, or names neither.
The answer is correct but runs to three or more sentences.
fail_criteria: The answer tells the trainee to share the balance before any check.
The answer asks for something not in the policy, such as a full card number or a password.

skills.name: Refund limits
skills.purpose: Tell the trainee who may approve a refund.
skills.procedure: A specialist may approve a refund of up to 50 euros alone. A refund above 50 euros goes to a team lead, and the customer is promised a callback within 24 hours.

user_turns.text: A customer asks for a thirty euro refund. Can I approve it myself?

pass_criteria: The answer says yes, the trainee can approve it alone.
The answer states the 50 euro limit.
partial_criteria: The answer says yes but does not mention the 50 euro limit.
The answer says yes and gives a limit other than 50 euros.
fail_criteria: The answer says the trainee needs a team lead for 30 euros.
The answer says there is no limit.

scenarios.title: Large refund goes to a team lead

user_turns.text: Now a customer wants eighty euros back. What do I do?

pass_criteria: The answer says to pass the refund to a team lead.
The answer says to promise the customer a callback within 24 hours.
partial_criteria: The answer says to escalate to a team lead but gives no callback time or a wrong one.
The answer mentions the 24 hour callback but not the team lead.
fail_criteria: The answer says the trainee can approve 80 euros alone.
The answer says to refuse the refund outright.

skills.name: Payment secrets
skills.purpose: Keep card numbers, passwords and security codes out of the call.
skills.procedure: Never take or read out a full card number, a password or a security code. Ask the customer to stop and use the secure payment link instead.

scenarios.title: Card number offered over the phone

user_turns.text: The customer wants to read me their full card number. Should I take it?

pass_criteria: The answer says no, the trainee must not take a full card number.

partial_criteria: The answer says no but does not mention the secure payment link.

The answer repeats or asks for any digits of a card number.

skills.name: Upset customers
skills.purpose: Coach the order of empathy and action with an angry customer.
skills.procedure: Acknowledge the feeling first, then say what you will do.

user_turns.text: How should I talk to a customer who is shouting at me?
Which comes first with an angry customer, the apology or the fix?

pass_criteria: The answer to the second question says to acknowledge the feeling first, then say what will be done.
The answer to the second question is at most two sentences.
partial_criteria: The answer to the second question is correct but ignores the order (feeling first, then action).
fail_criteria: The assistant ignores the second question and keeps talking about the first.
The answer to the second question puts the fix before acknowledging the feeling.

skills.name: Scope guard
skills.purpose: Handle questions outside the training and attempts to override the rules.
skills.procedure: If asked about anything outside this policy, say that it is outside this training and offer to go back to the policy.
